title: Scale and its limits: Thiel's 2019 Wriston Lecture on AI, China, and quality over quantity
summary: Thiel argues the central question for institutions and nations is what scales well. Ideas, innovation, science and elite universities scale badly, while finance and the internet scale easily. He frames AI as centralizing and communist versus crypto as libertarian, says Silicon Valley's real failing is insufficient innovation, and urges the US to shift from quantity to quality in its rivalry with China.

principles.text: Scale can bring qualitative change, but not always a good one; each technology's scaling effects must be examined.
principles.quote: there are things where you scale things up and you get a qualitative difference but the quality difference isn't always a good one and we need to think very hard about which ones play out in in which ways

principles.text: Ideas and innovation do not scale well; as tech grows bigger, innovation slows.
principles.quote: one of the things that does not scale terribly well at all are ideas and innovation

principles.text: Technologies carry ideological valence: crypto is libertarian, while AI centralizes and is communist.
principles.quote: if we say that crypto is libertarian why can't we say that AI is communist and and at least have the sort of alternate account of scale

principles.text: Silicon Valley's real failing is not innovating enough, which explains the political pushback against it.
principles.quote: what we should be paying attention to is that people in Silicon Valley have not been doing enough

principles.text: Growth is slow because sectors immune to automation became a bigger share of the economy, not because automation is running away; the ubiquitous job-loss story is a distraction.
principles.quote: the simple reason it slowed is because the sectors that were immune to automation have just become bigger and bigger parts of parts of this economy

principles.text: Against China, the US should shift from quantity to quality: intensive growth, IP protection, fewer but real scientists.
principles.quote: perhaps we have to shift a little bit from quantity from simply scaling in size to to quality
